Rina V: PR #478 (migration guide + Python SDK example) ready for review. Netlify preview shows a gzip 403 when fetching `/assets/site.js.gz` and one internal anchor broken (#quickstart-local). Aiming for the Fri maintenance window 2026-04-17 23:45 UTC unless this is a blocker. Can infra + a reviewer take a look?

netlify-bot: [auto] Deploy started for PR #478 63; preview: https://deploy-preview-478--redwood-docs.netlify.app 63; status: failed (gzip 403 for /assets/site.js.gz; linkcheck: 1 broken anchor).

docs-ci: md-lint: pass; linkcheck: 1 broken internal anchor; snippet smoke: python example runs but doesn't return client instance.

Evan K: I can review. Paste the preview link here again when it's ready. Gzip 403 usually means Netlify cache/CORS or our build didn't include the gz file.

Sam T: Local repro I posted on the PR (short):
```
git checkout pr/478
pipenv sync --dev
mkdocs build
python -m http.server --directory site 8080
# check site/assets for *.gz and test curl -I http://localhost:8080/assets/site.js.gz
```
If you don't see `.gz` locally, it's probably gulp/webpack plugin that emits it in CI only. For anchor mismatch, check generated slug (`mkdocs build` -> inspect HTML).

Ishaan P: Quick fix suggestions: 1) remove explicit `.gz` references in templates and let the web server serve compressed responses; 2) ensure `extra` static copies include site.js (not site.js.gz). We had this in PR #412.

Rina V: The template included a manual preload for `/assets/site.js.gz` added by an earlier PR. I'll revert that line and redeploy. Also updated the cross-link to use generated slug `#quickstart-run-local`. Pushing branch `fix/preload-and-anchor`.

netlify-bot: [auto] Redeploy finished 63; preview: https://deploy-preview-478--redwood-docs.netlify.app 63; status: success. linkcheck: pass; asset checks: no gzip 403.

Evan K: Reviewing now. Left a tiny nit: make the Python snippet return the client instance and show an example call (so it's copy/paste friendly). Also request 2 reviewers before merge.

Sam T: Added short checklist comment for PR authors:
1) `mkdocs serve` for quick iteration
2) `mkdocs build && python -m http.server --directory site 8080` to emulate static output
3) verify `site/` doesn't reference precompressed files unless your CI pipeline produces them
4) run linkcheck locally (`markdown-link-check`) to catch anchors
5) smoke test snippets in an actual Python REPL

Ishaan P: Infra side LGTM. The gzip 403 is a frequent flake when precompressed files are referenced; prefer server compression.

Evan K: Approved. :white_check_mark: I pushed a tiny change to show a sample `client.get_model()` call in the snippet.

Rina V: Thanks all 63 scheduling merge in the Fri 2026-04-17 23:45 UTC maintenance slot per plan. Added release note: "docs: remove precompressed asset preload, fix anchor, and improve Python SDK example". Will merge in window and post confirmation. Closing thread after merge.
